subject: Intermittent private control-channel failures after 11/08 upgrade
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@brightlane.health>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Brightlane Health NOC <noc@brightlane.health>
Date: Mon, 08 Nov 2027 20:07:12 -0800
Subject: Re: rolling upgrade completed — now seeing control channel blips

Hi Rishi / Laura,

We finished our validation pass this evening after your upgrade to the private control plane (11/08) and are seeing intermittent control-channel drops across two of our clusters in us-west-2. Symptoms: short-lived request timeouts (200–500ms extra) and a handful of 502s for model inference tasks. The issues started ~19:30 PT and have continued in waves since then.

I attached a short connection trace and a couple of example request IDs. Can you confirm whether anything in the upgrade could cause transient handshake retries, or if this looks environmental on our side? We need to know whether to pause traffic to the updated nodes while you investigate.

Pinged Tom on NOC; he can share more telemetry if useful.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Director, Platform Ops
Brightlane Health

Attachment: privatenet-connection-trace-20271108.log (text, 82KB)
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@brightlane.health>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 08 Nov 2027 20:33:01 -0800
Subject: Re: rolling upgrade completed — now seeing control channel blips

Elena — thanks for the heads up and the trace. Short answer: we saw an elevated rate of control-plane TLS renegotiations on the upgraded nodes during the first hour of the rollout; that would manifest as additional handshake RTT and occasional 502s if retries coincided with backend transitions.

Immediate plan:
- We will open a private bridge with your NOC and our infra team to correlate traces (propose 20:45 PT).
- I'll ask engineering to snapshot node metrics and roll a targeted minor config that reduces TLS session renegotiation frequency; it’s low-risk and reversible.
- Please keep traffic to the affected pool throttled to the safe baseline if you can (status page shows ~2.5k rps right now).

I'll be on the bridge and will update here after the first mitigation.

Apologies for the disruption — we aim for zero-customer visible impact on upgrades and missed that goal here.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachment: upgrade-notes-20271108.pdf (summary of changes applied during rollout)
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@brightlane.health>, Brightlane Health NOC <noc@brightlane.health>
Date: Tue, 09 Nov 2027 08:12:46 -0800
Subject: Re: rolling upgrade completed — now seeing control channel blips

Hi all — quick tech update from infra after correlating the traces on the bridge this morning.

What we found:
- Root cause: an interaction between the new TLS session ticket rotation window in the 11/08 runtime build and Brightlane's connection churn pattern. The rotation frequency caused additional short-lived TLS handshakes during peak switchovers (control-plane leadership changes).
- Impact: handshake retries increased median control-plane RTT by ~240ms for affected flows; in collision cases with the request proxy, that produced 502 responses.

Mitigation applied (09:05 PT):
- We rolled back the session-ticket rotation parameter to the previous stable value for Brightlane's dedicated node pool.
- We disabled the aggressive ticket refresh on the remaining nodes until we can ship a fix.

Status now:
- Observed error rates dropped to baseline within ~6 minutes of rollback. Brightlane NOC confirmed a return to normal for the two impacted clusters.

Next steps:
1) Engineering will prepare a patch that retains the security intent of the rotation change while adding a jittered timer and cluster-aware backoff (ETA for patch: 2027-11-12 EOD).
2) We will schedule a short maintenance window with Brightlane (30 min) to test the patch in canary and then roll to the rest of their nodes.
3) We'll produce a short post-incident write-up and a recommended upgrade checklist for Brightlane private deployments to avoid similar collisions.

Thanks to Elena and Tom for fast triage. I’ll add logs and a short root-cause note to SUP-4821.

—Mina Haddad
Principal Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Follow-up: incident resolved, next steps and offer of credit

Elena / Tom — thanks again for working with us on the bridge this morning. Short summary for your ops and exec teams:

What happened: a new session-ticket rotation parameter in our 11/08 private control-plane build interacted with Brightlane's connection churn and control-plane leadership changes, increasing TLS handshake frequency and producing transient 502s for a subset of requests.

What we did: rolled the parameter back for Brightlane’s node pool, disabled aggressive refresh globally for remaining private nodes, and deployed a short-term mitigant that restored baseline within minutes.

Next steps and timeline:
- Engineering patch with jittered rotation and cluster-aware backoff: target 2027-11-12 EOD.
- We will schedule a 30-minute canary maintenance window with you on 11/13 to validate the patch, then roll to the remaining Brightlane nodes if successful.
- Post-incident report with RCA and checklist will be delivered by 11/15.

Customer impact and remediation: we recognize this caused visible errors for some Brightlane requests during peak evening traffic. As discussed on the bridge, Redwood will:
- Credit Brightlane for the impacted hour (one hour of Dedicated capacity) and apply it to your next billing statement.
- Offer an optional 1:1 postmortem review with our infra leads and your SREs to walk the patch and checklist.

If you'd like us to throttle traffic further during patch validation or to perform the canary outside your peak window, tell us your preferred times and we'll accommodate.

Apologies again — we value the reliability of your private deployment and will take steps to prevent regressions like this.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Director of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
